title: Nonhuman Primate Lung Decellularization and Recellularization Using a Specialized Large-organ Bioreactor
protocol: Autoclave 10-15 L of deionized water in 1-2 L bottles.
Mix 1 ml Triton X-100 in 999 ml of deionized water while stirring on a magnetic stirrer to prepare the "Triton solution".
Filter the "Triton solution" through a 0.22 μm filter apparatus.
Store the "Triton solution" at room temperature.
Slowly add 20 g of sodium deoxycholate (SDC) to ~900 ml of deionized water while stirring to prepare the "SDC solution".
Transfer the SDC solution to a graduated cylinder and bring the volume to 1 L with deionized water.
Filter the "SDC solution" through a 0.22 μm filter apparatus.
Store the "SDC solution" at room temperature.
Add 58 g of NaCl to ~900 ml of deionized water and stir until completely dissolved to prepare the "NaCl solution".
Add deionized water to bring the volume to 1 L for the "NaCl solution", then filter it.
Store the "NaCl solution" at room temperature.
Put on a surgical mask, face shield, surgical gloves, disposable gown, and a second layer of surgical gloves before handling nonhuman primate tissues.
Collect intact heart-lung blocs from animal necropsy in PBS containing 50 U/ml heparin to prevent coagulation of external blood.
Cannulate the pulmonary artery using a female Luer connector with an appropriately sized barb while the lungs lie flat in a dissecting tray.
Secure the cannula in place with an alcohol-sterilized zip tie.
Slip a sterile zip tie around the trachea.
Insert a 0.250 in female Luer connector into the tracheal opening.
Tighten the zip tie around the barb of the connector to hold the trachea in place.
Instill PBS containing 30 U/ml heparin and 5 µg/ml sodium nitroprusside (SNP) into the lungs.
Allow the solution to be expelled by natural recoil.
Repeat instillation twice more.
Cap the tracheal Luer cannula with a Luer plug after the third instillation.
Cut off the apex of the heart.
Irrigate internal ventricles with PBS-heparin-SNP to remove residual blood.
Lacerate both atria to facilitate drainage upon perfusion.
Submerge the heart-lung bloc in dH2O.
Fill a 60 ml syringe with the PBS-heparin-SNP solution.
Submerge the arterial cannula so that all air bubbles escape from the vascular opening.
Attach the filled syringe and carefully remove the plunger to allow liquid into the vasculature.
Remove the plug from the tracheal cannula to expel fluid in the airway by natural recoil.
Continue to add PBS-heparin-SNP solution to maintain ~15-20 cm H2O pressure above the artery during perfusion.
Continue perfusion until as much blood as possible is removed from the pulmonary vasculature.
Submerge the heart-lung bloc in dH2O.
Inflate and perfuse the lung with dH2O using 60 ml syringes attached to the submerged tracheal and arterial cannulae, respectively.
Repeat airway and vascular washes with dH2O four times for a total of five rinses.
Remove the lungs from water and submerge the bloc in Triton solution.
Inflate and perfuse the lungs with Triton solution as before.
Incubate the submerged organs in Triton solution overnight at 4 °C.
Remove the lung bloc from Triton solution after overnight incubation.
Wash externally with dH2O.
Submerge the bloc in fresh dH2O.
Repeat dH2O washes five times.
Remove the lungs from dH2O and submerge in SDC solution.
Inflate and perfuse with SDC solution in the same manner as before.
Incubate submerged in SDC solution overnight at 4 °C.
Wash the tissue again with dH2O after overnight incubation.
Remove the tissue from dH2O and submerge in NaCl solution.
Inflate and perfuse with NaCl solution in the same manner as before.
Incubate submerged in NaCl solution for 1 hour at room temperature.
Wash the lungs clean of NaCl solution with dH2O.
Prepare fresh "DNase solution".
Bathe the lungs in DNase solution.
Instill DNase solution into the airway and vasculature.
Incubate the lungs in DNase solution for 1 hour at room temperature.
Prepare fresh PBS solution (1x PBS + 5x antibiotic/antimycotic).
Remove lungs from DNase solution.
Wash external surface of lungs with PBS solution.
Submerge lungs in PBS solution and wash five times.
Store lungs in PBS solution overnight at 4 °C.
On the next day, wash lungs in fresh ice-cold PBS solution five times.
Store lungs in PBS solution in a sterile sealed container at 4 °C until use.
Assemble breathing loop and vascular loop structures ahead of time.
Autoclave all bioreactor components except for sterile-packaged air filters and syringe ports.
Assemble bioreactor components under a laminar flow hood according to the schematic.
Fill main chamber with culture medium equilibrated to 5% CO2 atmosphere.
Apply tracheal and vascular cannulae adapters to lung cannulae.
Install lungs in the main bioreactor chamber by bathing in culture medium.
Attach cannulae adapters to appropriate ports in the modified lid.
Affix the lid securely and tightly.
Fill the tracheal reservoir approximately half-full with culture medium and affix the modified cap.
Apply sterile 0.22 µm syringe filters, Luer plugs, and syringe ports to all chambers as indicated.
Connect the trachea reservoir to the main chamber via the breathing loop apparatus.
Attach the breathing loop tubing as indicated.
Aspirate air from the tubing using a 60 ml syringe fitted with an 18 G needle and move the directionality of the 3-way stopcocks.
Move the sealed, contiguously connected bioreactor chambers to a tissue culture incubator to equilibrate temperature and gas.
Ventilate the lungs using a syringe pump attached to the main chamber at approximately 1 breath every 2 min.
Perfuse the vasculature via the peristaltic pump at approximately 10 ml/min for about 30 minutes.
Prepare suspensions of cells to be seeded into the airway at the desired cell density.
Inflate the lungs with the cell suspension by gently injecting through the syringe port attached to the three-way stopcock in the breathing loop.
Hold the lungs statically at 37 °C, 5% CO2 overnight without perfusion to allow cells to attach.
Reinitiate the standard airway ventilation program after overnight incubation.
Culture the organs for 3-7 days or as desired.
Prepare suspensions of endothelial cell cultures.
Transfer the cell suspension to the endothelial-seeding reservoir containing a magnetic stir bar.
Rotate the valve on the stopcock connecting the main chamber and endothelial seeding reservoir.
Seed endothelial cells gradually using a peristaltic pump while stirring gently.
Incubate statically for approximately 4-6 hours after seeding is complete.
Reinitiate vascular perfusion with main chamber medium at a rate of ~10 ml/min.
Culture for 3-7 days with continuous vascular perfusion.
Remove blood by pulmonary artery perfusion in cadaveric animals.
Expel fluids from the lungs after cells are lysed during decellularization.
Incubate lungs overnight at 4 °C while submerged in instilled fluid to expel viscous fluid.
Proceed with instillation of subsequent solutions if necessary after allowing as much fluid to be expelled as possible.
Add detergents and deionized water washes to facilitate removal of viscous fluids.
